newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Sri Lanka's Miri crude tender saw no offers - CPC.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka's Miri crude tender saw no offers - CPC.

text.p: Sri Lankan state-owned Ceylon Petroleum Corp's (CPC) tender to buy 450,000 barrels of Malaysia's light-sweet Miri crude for December 10-12 delivery has attracted no offers, a CPC official said on Friday.
"There has been no offers of Miri crude in the tender," the official said. The tender closed on November 13 with validity until Friday.

Since it received no Miri offers, Sri Lanka on Thursday switched its tender requirements to light Middle East crudes. But as the tender was only valid until Friday, sellers did not put in any offers due to the short notice, the official said.
"We may now buy Iranian or Arabian light crudes from our term supplier for delivery in December," he said.

Sri Lanka had initially issued the tender for Miri after it has used up its contractual volume of the Malaysian crude from state-owned Petronas for 1996 and required a spot cargo to top up its storage tanks.
Petronas has a one-year contract to supply 300,000 tonnes of Miri crude for Sri Lanka's 60,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) Sapugaskanda refinery.

The final shipment of 450,000 barrels from the term contract was discharged at the refinery at the end of October. The spot Miri cargo which CPC sought was intended to tide it over until the end of the year.
The official said its term talks for 1997 will only start sometime in December or January and the volume is expected to remain at 300,000 tonnes.

Regional traders said there are few spot Miri cargoes in the market as most of them have been committed to term buyers. The term lifters are restricted under certain clause from reselling the cargoes.
Any available spot Miri cargoes are sold to Singapore refiners and other buyers in the Far East
December Miri prices on a free-on-board Malaysia basis were assessed on Friday at $24.75 per barrel and at a $1.20-premium to published quotes based on the most recent spot deal done for December.
